idiom_name: typed worker pool and message protocol over the event loop
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits the JavaScript host model: the event loop is the asynchronous layer, worker_threads or libuv's internal pool is the synchronous layer, and async/await carries the eventual result as Promise<T>. What the type system adds is the boundary contract - model queue messages as discriminated unions so the asynchronous layer cannot enqueue a shape no worker handles, and type the worker's response so the join back into the promise is checked - which removes the most common failure of this pattern in practice. Downlevel async emit adds helper machinery but does not change the layering; the explicit worker pool is still justified for CPU-bound stages, where it is the only way to use more than one core.
pitfalls: A worker's message channel has no back-pressure: track outstanding promises and throttle, the in-flight set grows otherwise.
Types do not survive postMessage; the message must be narrowed or validated in the worker instead of being cast with as any.
Importing a synchronous native addon on the main thread blocks the event loop even though the surrounding code is async.
One shared Worker receiving interleaved jobs needs a correlation id, otherwise responses are resolved against the wrong request.
